title: IQM and AMD Demonstrate Reproducible Hybrid QPU-GPU Chemistry Workflow Using ROCm - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Workflow diagram showing how the work is split between the IQM quantum computer and the AMD GPU.

IQM Quantum Computers (Nasdaq: IQMX) and AMD have demonstrated an end-to-end hybrid quantum-classical computational chemistry workflow that partitions molecular ground-state energy calculations across IQM’s 20-qubit superconducting IQM Garnet processor and AMD Instinct GPUs running the open-source ROCm software stack. Detailed in the first installment of a planned technical series, the collaboration establishes a multi-vendor alternative for supercomputing centers integrating quantum processors with classical GPU accelerators.

The workflow implements Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI) to bypass the exponential memory scaling of exact classical diagonalization. Accessed via the IQM Resonance cloud platform, the Garnet processor prepares a parameterized trial circuit and samples bitstrings to identify dominant electron configurations, while an AMD GPU filters unphysical samples, constructs the projected subspace Hamiltonian, and executes cubic-scaling (O(N3)) matrix diagonalization using JAX on ROCm.

The teams validated the full pipeline on molecular hydrogen (H2 in the minimal STO-3G basis), reproducing the dissociation curve across 17 bond lengths on physical hardware while resolving ROCm version-pinning dependencies for hybrid execution. Candidly framed as an interoperability validation rather than a demonstration of quantum advantage, the workflow is available as an open-source Jupyter notebook on IQM Academy for execution on AMD Developer Cloud GPU instances as the partners work toward tighter physical interconnects and larger molecular active spaces above eight qubits.
